A1.justification: Both PDFs provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices for the same research work. The model is renamed from Vid-ICL to VidIT, but corresponding methods and experiments can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original SSv2 quantitative experiments, human evaluations, scaling studies and ablations, plus RT-1 generation examples and VP2 simulation trajectories in Appendix A.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds baseline evaluations, FVD measurements, MineRL and VIPSeg demonstrations, and failure and attention analyses.

M1.justification: The VQ tokenizer, LLaMA architecture, next-token objective and core demonstration-conditioned generation procedure remain unchanged. V2 adds a limited segmentation adaptation using VIPSeg fine-tuning and video/segmentation demonstration pairs, extending generation to segmentation outputs (Section 5.4; Appendix A.2).

E1.justification: V2 adds MineRL gameplay tasks, specifically chopping wood and attacking sheep, and VIPSeg video segmentation, substantially extending task and environment coverage. RT-1 and VP2 already appear in v1's appendix. An actual replacement of WebVid training data is unresolved: v2 describes self-collected videos but retains WebVid in Table 9.

E2.justification: The principal comparison expands from DeLVM alone in v1 Table 3 to DeLVM, LVM and LWM in v2 Table 2, with further metrics in Table 6. LVM and LWM were previously cited but not evaluated in this comparison. SVG remains the comparator for the retained VP2 example.

E3.justification: V2 adds FVD and a VIPSeg evaluation following task-specific fine-tuning. Its new Figure 8 compares 7B LVM/LWM with 1.1B VidIT. The core SSv2 split, frame configuration and 10-user, 20-pair human evaluation remain unchanged. Removal of v1's explicit eight-frame DeLVM matching description does not establish an actual change to that experiment.

E4.justification: Appendices A.3-A.5 add comparative generation case studies, explicit failure examples, training-versus-inference attention visualizations and successful-versus-failed prompting attention distributions. Conversely, v1's WebVid data-volume ablation and perplexity plot are removed. Demonstration-length/count and text-conditioning ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. Both retain the same practice of reporting point estimates and average human ratings; attention-head averaging in v2 is not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Existing Table 1 metrics, scaling curves and DeLVM/proposed-model comparison scores are retained. V2 adds FVD results, including 125.77 for pretrained in-class prompting, LVM/LWM P-Acc scores of 27.1/24.9, fuller baseline metrics, and MineRL, segmentation, failure and attention findings. V1's WebVid perplexity results are removed. These additions do not establish improved performance of the proposed model under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical conditioning definitions and autoregressive formulations in Equations (1)-(4) are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v2's attention analysis is empirical rather than a new mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: The central claims of zero-shot demonstration-guided video generation, scaling behavior and multimodal prompting remain. V2 drops the abstract's explicit claim of analyzing the effects of different training datasets. Its imitation terminology largely reframes the retained capabilities rather than establishing a different central scientific claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds attention-based explanations connecting transfer to similar object-focused attention and failures to ignoring demonstrations, refining v1's general discussion of semantic guidance. It removes the WebVid-scaling interpretation. The original limitations concerning longer sequences and unreliable demonstrations are retained and relocated to Appendix C.

D1.justification: V2 reports code/model release, whereas v1 states there are no current plans for public access. Appendix B.4 newly discloses 16 H100 GPUs, PyTorch DDP/Lightning, 15 epochs and 720 GPU-hours; these are disclosures, not established training changes. V2 also names a VideoMAE checkpoint, but leaves its Kinetics name unreconciled with the stated SSv2-trained classifier. V1's explicit matched DeLVM frame and parameter settings are omitted.

R1.justification: V2 substantially reframes the research around imitation learning, introduces reinforcement-learning imitation background and emphasizes self-supervised training relative to supervised image-prompting methods. It adds citations for the imitation-learning survey, RT-1, VIPSeg, FVD and SVG, removes the WebVid reference, and gives the already-cited LWM a substantive comparator role.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and opening motivation are extensively rewritten around video imitation, with VidIT terminology throughout. Related work is reorganized, a Generalization Ability section is introduced, and Appendix A gains six subsections. Limitations move to the appendix, while broader-impact and ethics discussions are consolidated.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 6-11 and a full baseline-metrics table, expands Table 1 with FVD, and restructures the baseline comparison display. Figure 1 incorporates existing RT-1 examples, and another RT-1 panel is promoted into the main text. The WebVid plot is removed. The original SSv2 and RT-1 appendix sample panels are retained as Tables 10-11.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens validation through actual LVM/LWM comparisons and video-level FVD measurements, while failure examples and attention analyses make the model's behavior more inspectable. Compute disclosures and the reported code/model release also help reproducibility. The net gain is limited by removal of the WebVid ablation and explicit DeLVM matching details, ambiguous training-data and classifier descriptions, and the qualitative nature of the new generalization demonstrations.
